defects.description: The new key's plaintext secret is stored in a pending_secret TEXT column, violating the NFR that plaintext secrets are never written to the database unencrypted.

The secret endpoint returns pending_secret on every call until the hourly job clears it, so the secret can be fetched repeatedly and for up to ~70 minutes. R7/AC4 require one retrieval only, within 10 minutes, then 404.
Plan adds a new src/lib/parseHours.ts helper instead of using the existing intParam in src/lib/validate.ts that routes already use for integer body params.
grace_period_hours above 168 is capped, negatives become 0, and non-numeric values fall back to 24. Spec R3/AC2 require 400 (and no key created) for any value that is not an integer in 0-168.

Inline authorization allows any org_admin without comparing key.orgId to actor.orgId, so admins of other orgs can rotate keys (violates R4/AC5). It also duplicates KeyService.assertCanManage, which already does the correct check.
defects.location: plan.md step 4; fixture/src/keys/keyService.ts; spec.md R4, AC5

defects.description: Rotate checks status then creates the replacement and marks rotating as separate non-transactional steps, so concurrent rotate requests can both pass the status check and create two replacement keys (violates the concurrency NFR and R5).
defects.location: plan.md step 5; spec.md R5, non-functional constraints

defects.description: verify accepts any key with status 'rotating' without checking grace_ends_at; the old key keeps working until the hourly expireDue run, up to an hour past graceEndsAt, violating R2/AC1 and the one-minute NFR. AC1 is only checked by observing staging.
defects.location: plan.md steps 6 and test strategy; fixture/src/server.ts; spec.md R2, AC1

tensions.description: Risk's natural fix is to stop persisting the plaintext secret at all (drop pending_secret). That removes the only mechanism for R7's re-display. Consistency wants R7 implemented more strictly (once, within 10 minutes), which presupposes the secret is still retrievable server-side. The two fixes pull in opposite directions unless someone notices the NFR only forbids unencrypted storage and the fixture already has encrypt/decrypt.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Remove the pending_secret column; never store the new secret anywhere after the response.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Enforce R7 at read time: return the secret only once and only within 10 minutes of rotation.
tensions.reconciliation: Store the new secret encrypted with lib/crypto encrypt() plus an expires_at of rotation + 10 minutes; on GET, atomically read-and-delete it (UPDATE ... SET pending_secret = NULL ... RETURNING) only when unexpired and the caller is the rotating actor, and clear expired values. This satisfies both the NFR and R7/AC4.

tensions.description: Architecture's natural fix is to drop parseHours and reuse validate.intParam. But intParam is lenient by design: it clamps out-of-range values into [min, max] and returns the default for non-numeric input, exactly the behaviour consistency flags as contradicting R3 (400 on invalid). Reusing it as-is keeps the spec violation. Visible only in validate.ts.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Replace parseHours with intParam(raw, { min: 0, max: 168, default: 24 }).
tensions.lens_b_fix: Reject non-integer, negative, or >168 values with 400 before creating any key.
tensions.reconciliation: Add a strict variant to validate.ts (e.g. intParam with a strict flag, or a strictIntParam that throws a 400 error) without changing intParam's lenient default for existing callers, and use it for grace_period_hours; test AC2.
